## Schema, migrations & scripts

### 2026-05-20: `prisma migrate dev` traps — advisory lock from a backgrounded run; non-interactive refusal on warnings
tags: entities=migration,prisma · files=packages/data/package.json,packages/data/prisma/schema.prisma · track=028
**Problem:** Two ways `migrate dev` (wrapped by `npm run migrate:local`) wedges in an agent shell. (1) Backgrounded, it holds the Postgres advisory lock while waiting on its name prompt; a second `migrate dev` fails at once with `P1002`. (2) When Prisma wants to warn (data loss, `@unique` on a populated column) it refuses the non-interactive shell outright — neither `--name` nor piping the answer on stdin gets past "non-interactive environment not supported".
**Solution:** (1) `pkill -f "prisma migrate dev"`, then run in the foreground with the name piped: `echo "name" | npx prisma migrate dev`. (2) Generate the SQL yourself and deploy it: `npx prisma migrate diff --from-config-datasource --to-schema ./prisma/schema.prisma --script > prisma/migrations/$(date -u +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)_<name>/migration.sql`, READ it (must be additive), then `npx prisma migrate deploy` (local) → `npx prisma generate` → `npm run migrate:integration` (sunbnb_test) → `npm run migrate:check` must report "No difference detected". Same end state as `migrate:local`.
**Prevention:** Never background `migrate dev`. Never hand-edit a `migration.sql` after it has been applied (`.claude/rules/migrations.md`). Reach for the `migrate diff --script` path as soon as a schema change will trigger a Prisma warning.

### 2026-06-14: --create-only migration pattern for custom backfills
tags: entities=migration,backfill · files=packages/data/package.json,packages/data/prisma/migrations
**Problem:** `migrate:local` auto-applies. A migration that needs an idempotent data backfill appended to the generated SQL would run before the backfill could be added.
**Solution:** `echo "name" | npx prisma migrate dev --create-only --name <name>` to generate the file, append the backfill SQL, apply with `echo "" | npx prisma migrate dev`, then `npm run migrate:integration` to keep `sunbnb_test` in lockstep (what `migrate:local` would have done).
**Prevention:** Any migration carrying seed/backfill data uses `--create-only`. Backfill SQL is idempotent (`ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` / `WHERE col IS NULL`). Deterministic IDs (`'grp_' || LEAST(a, b)`) beat `gen_random_uuid()` inside CTEs — no correlation problems, no extension.

### 2026-06-14: SunbedGroup model — additive, mocks updated in partner + user; admin skipped
tags: entities=inventory,sunbed-group,mocks · files=packages/data/prisma/schema.prisma,apps/partner/__mocks__/@repo/data/PrismaCient.ts,apps/user/__mocks__/@repo/data/PrismaCient.ts,packages/data/src/test/fixtures.ts
**Problem:** Adding the `SunbedGroup` model (+ nullable `InventoryItem.sunbedGroupId`, `Site.sunbedGroups[]`) crashed partner and user test files at import time — the Prisma mocks had no `sunbedGroup` delegate.
**Solution:** Added the delegate to both `apps/partner` and `apps/user` `__mocks__/@repo/data/PrismaCient.ts`; `apps/admin` skipped (never touches inventory). `packages/data/src/test/fixtures.ts` got `createTestSunbedGroup()`.
**Prevention:** Any new top-level model that partner or user code might query must appear in both those mocks, even when no test calls it yet — a missing delegate fails the whole file at import.

### 2026-07-18: One-open-tab-per-table guard — unique-when-active column, not a partial unique index
tags: entities=table-tab,dine-in,migration,prisma · files=packages/data/prisma/schema.prisma,packages/data/prisma/migrations/20260718095626_add_table_tab_dine_in/migration.sql · track=002
**Problem:** The find-or-create guard "exactly one OPEN `TableTab` per table" wants a partial unique index (`WHERE status = 'open'`). Prisma Schema cannot express partial indexes, so a hand-written one leaves `migrate:check` permanently red.
**Solution:** `TableTab.openTableId String? @unique` — set to `tableId` while open, NULLed by every closing path in the same update that writes the terminal status. NULLs never collide, so a plain unique index enforces the invariant; the loser of a concurrent create re-reads and joins the winner's tab (`schema.prisma#TableTab`).
**Prevention:** When an invariant needs "unique among active rows", model a nullable unique column that is non-null only while active. Audit every path that flips the row inactive — forgetting to NULL the column blocks the next open.

### 2026-07-10: $queryRaw requires quoted camelCase for un-mapped Prisma columns
tags: entities=backfill,raw-sql,prisma · files=packages/data/scripts
**Problem:** Prisma fields without `@map()` (`createdAt`, `updatedAt`, …) are stored under their camelCase name. Raw SQL `r.created_at` fails with `column does not exist` (42703) — the column is `"createdAt"`.
**Solution:** Double-quote unmapped camelCase columns in `$queryRaw` (`r."createdAt"`); fields with `@map("snake_case")` use the mapped name unquoted.
**Prevention:** Before writing `$queryRaw` against a model, check the exact column names (`\d "TableName"` in psql or the `@map` in `schema.prisma`).

### 2026-10-13: Dropping a table — the integration setups truncate it by name
tags: entities=schema,migration,test · files=packages/data/src/test/setup.ts,apps/partner/app/test/setup.ts,apps/user/app/test/setup.ts · track=032
**Problem:** a contract migration dropped `"Settlement"`; unit suites and typechecks were green, but promote aborted at the integration gate — every integration file failed with `42P01 relation does not exist`.
**Solution:** three hand-written `cleanDatabase` TRUNCATE lists name tables explicitly; remove the dropped table from all three (and any raw SQL in tests, e.g. the assistant-reader denied-table list).
**Prevention:** before committing a drop/rename, `grep -rn '"<Table>"'` across `apps/*/app/test` and `packages/data/src` with no `head` cap, and run `npm run test:integration` in data, partner and user — unit tests never touch the setup.

## Payment / invoice / fee / subscription

### 2026-05-20: effective-subscription resolution convention (CustomSubscription)
tags: entities=subscription,custom-subscription · files=packages/data/src/subscription.ts
**Problem:** Need one canonical way to merge a partner's base `SubscriptionPlan` with a sparse `CustomSubscription` override (null field = inherit base).
**Solution:** `resolveEffectiveSubscription(plan, custom)` in `src/subscription.ts` — pure. Custom non-null wins → plan → hard defaults (STARTER, maxSites=1, price=0). `isCustom` only when the custom record has non-null `maxSites`. `canCreateSite` does one `partnerAccount.findUnique` selecting `customSubscription` + `subscription.plan`, then calls the helper.
**Prevention:** Every per-partner plan override goes through `resolveEffectiveSubscription` (add nullable fields to `CustomSubscription`, extend the helper). Never derive limits from `subscription.plan` alone.

### 2026-05-20: feature entitlements — catalog/resolver pattern + circular import avoidance
tags: entities=subscription,feature-flags,fee-context · files=packages/data/src/subscription.ts,packages/data/src/payment.ts
**Problem:** Wiring the feature catalog (`SUBSCRIPTION_FEATURES`, `resolveEffectiveFeatures`) into fee contexts risked a `payment.ts` ↔ `subscription.ts` import cycle.
**Solution:** The resolver is pure and lives in `subscription.ts`; `payment.ts` imports it, never the reverse. `CustomSubscription.featureOverrides` is `Json?` — cast at the DB boundary. `SiteFeeContext`/`PartnerFeeContext` gained `features: Record<SubscriptionFeatureKey, boolean>`; both loaders include `customSubscription`.
**Prevention:** Keep the resolver pure in `subscription.ts`; cast Prisma `Json` at the boundary, not inside helpers. A new feature is a one-liner in the catalog + tier defaults — no migration (sparse JSON map).

### 2026-06-20: rental-payment.ts — list-based create, single-id verify/finalize for RentalBooking
tags: entities=rental-booking,mollie,payment · files=packages/data/src/rental-payment.ts,packages/data/package.json
**Pattern:** `createRentalBookingMolliePayment(bookingIds, opts)` takes 1–20 ids sharing a `siteId`; amount = `round(sum paymentAmount)` from the DB; ONE Mollie payment, same `paymentRef` + `RENTAL_PROCESSING` on all via `updateMany`; provider failure → all `RENTAL_PAYMENT_FAILED`. Status/finalize helpers are single-booking, but `reverifyAndFinalizeRentalBooking` delegates to the group-keyed `processConfirmedRentalBooking(paymentRef)`, so finalizing any representative closes the group.
**Prevention:** When the create path uses `updateMany`, the error path must too (`{ id: { in: bookingIds } }`). The user app's `/api/payment/mollie/create-rental-payment/route.ts` is an independent implementation (`mollie-app-fee`), not a caller of this module.

### 2026-07-10: processConfirmedReservation opts — skipCommission (cash receipt) + invoicedAt
tags: entities=invoice,cash-receipt,reservation,commission · files=packages/data/src/payment.ts,packages/data/src/invoice-series.ts
**Pattern:** `ProcessReservationOpts { skipCommission?, invoicedAt?, skipEmail? }`. Cash/walk-in: `skipCommission: true` creates one PARTNER invoice, skips the PLATFORM invoice AND skips the `status = RESERVATION_COMPLETE` mutation (stays `'paid-in-cash'`). `invoicedAt` back-dates the invoice; numbering is per issuer/series in `src/invoice-series.ts` (track 026), which takes the year from `invoicedAt`, so a backfilled June sale numbers into the right year.
**Critical:** The status update inside the transaction MUST stay gated on `!skipCommission` — otherwise a cash reservation flips to `complete` and the manage grid can no longer tell cash from online. The existing `invoices.length > 0` guard (re-checked inside the transaction) already makes cash receipts idempotent.
**Prevention:** Never add `RESERVATION_PAID_IN_CASH` to `PAID_STATUSES` — paid-in-cash deliberately sits outside the COMPLETE cycle so settlement can distinguish cash from online.

### 2026-07-13: cancelReservationMolliePayment — 422→paid semantics, slim token lookup, Viva delegation
tags: entities=reservation,mollie,viva,payment-cancel · files=packages/data/src/reservation-payment.ts
**Pattern:** `cancelReservationMolliePayment(reservationId, cashRegisterId?)` only talks to the provider; the caller (partner `cancelCollection`) owns all local state from the returned status. Mollie 422 = payment no longer `open` (consumer paid while the abandon was in flight) → return `{ status: 'paid' }` so the caller finalizes instead of deleting. No `paymentRef` / demo ref → `{ status: 'canceled' }` with no call. A `viva_` ref short-circuits into `cancelReservationVivaPayment` — the exported name stays Mollie-specific (every app imports the path; same discipline as `./PrismaCient`).
**Token lookup:** `partnerAccount.findUnique({ where: { userId: site.userId } })` with a two-field reservation select (`paymentRef`, `site.userId`) — NOT `loadFeeContext` (fees/subscription/settings are irrelevant to a cancel).
**Test mocking:** both `prisma.reservation.findUnique` and `prisma.partnerAccount.findUnique` mocks must be declared via `vi.hoisted()` before the `vi.mock('../index', …)` factory, or it closes over uninitialized bindings.

### 2026-10-07: Stripe Connect data layer (P3a) — what the canon does not say
tags: entities=stripe,stripe-connect,platform-invoice,fee-policy · files=packages/data/src/stripe/client.ts,packages/data/src/payment.ts,packages/data/src/payment-providers/fee-policy.ts,packages/data/src/payment-providers/index.ts · track=028
**Pattern:** (Structure — direct charges, pass-through, table deposits — is canon in `packages/data/CLAUDE.md` § Payment providers.) The `stripe` SDK is imported only in `src/stripe/{client,connect,checkout}.ts`; tests mock `./client` (`getStripeClient` / `getStripeConnectClient`), never the `stripe` package. A zero-commission Stripe payment still gets a PLATFORM invoice with only the `payment-processing` line (`totalServiceFee > 0 || passThrough > 0` gate in every `processConfirmed*`); zero-commission Mollie stays invoice-less. `fee-policy.ts` caps the application fee at `amount - 0.01`, `platformPassThroughFor` is uncapped — they diverge only for sub-EUR amounts.
**Prevention:** `payment-providers/index.ts` pulls in `stripe-adapter` (server-only) — client components import `/types`, `/availability`, `/readiness`, never the barrel (same split rule as every `@repo/data` submodule a client touches).

### 2026-10-08: cardPresent 'tap-to-pay' is a kind, not a provider — Mollie reports it too
tags: entities=card-present,tap-to-pay,stripe-terminal,mollie,availability · files=packages/data/src/payment-providers/availability.ts,packages/data/src/reservation-machine-apply.ts,apps/mobile/src/lib/site-context.ts · track=028
**Problem:** `PROVIDER_AVAILABILITY` returns `cardPresent: 'tap-to-pay'` for Mollie in NL BE DE FI PL PT CH DK LU (Mollie's own Tap to Pay on iPhone) as well as for Stripe. A consumer that treats `'tap-to-pay'` as "wire the Stripe Terminal SDK" misfires on a Mollie site.
**Solution:** Gate Stripe Terminal on `paymentProvider === 'stripe' && cardPresent === 'tap-to-pay'` (`apps/mobile/src/lib/site-context.ts`). Server-side, `runCollectStartTapToPay` returns `effect-failed` (`'venue has not connected Stripe'`) when the partner lacks `stripeConnectChargesEnabled`/`stripeConnectAccountId`.
**Prevention:** `CardPresentKind` describes how staff can take a card, not which rail; any new card-present consumer pairs it with `Site.paymentProvider` before picking an SDK.

## Reservations

### 2026-06-16: reserveWithConflictGuard — FOR UPDATE on InventoryItem, structured conflict return
tags: entities=reservation,inventory,conflict-guard,double-booking · files=packages/data/src/reservations.ts,packages/data/src/reservations.integration.test.ts
**Problem:** Partner and user call sites did conflict-check then create as two awaits — concurrent requests both passed and double-booked.
**Solution:** `reserveWithConflictGuard` (`@repo/data/reservations`): interactive `$transaction` → `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` on the candidate `InventoryItem` rows (the bed, not the not-yet-existing reservation) → `tx.reservation.findFirst` → `tx.reservation.create`. Returns `{ outcome: 'created' | 'conflict' }` — never throws for a business conflict (a throw inside `$transaction` reads as a DB error). `blockingStatuses` defaults to `BLOCKING_STATUSES`; partner call sites historically used `notIn [CANCELED]` (also blocks PAYMENT_FAILED/REFUNDED) — pass a custom list to match. The race test fires two claims via `Promise.all` and asserts one created, one conflict, one row.
**Prevention:** Expand SunbedGroup + pair siblings BEFORE calling — the helper does not expand items (caller responsibility, matches the existing call-site pattern).

## Viva card-present (track 024)

### 2026-08-30: Viva Cloud Terminal client (A1) — stub/http split, shared fee guard, spec beats brief
tags: entities=viva,cloud-terminal,isv-fee,stub-client · files=packages/data/src/viva/types.ts,packages/data/src/viva/refs.ts,packages/data/src/viva/http-client.ts,packages/data/src/viva/stub-client.ts,packages/data/src/viva/index.ts · track=024
**Pattern:** `VivaClient` (`createSale`/`getSession`/`abortSession`/`refund`/`searchDevices`) with two implementations picked by `getVivaClient()` (`VIVA_MODE`; stub when unset and no `VIVA_ISV_CLIENT_ID`). The fee guard (`isvDetails.amount` must be `> 0` and `< amount` — Viva declines a fee ≥ the sale) is ONE shared pure function, `assertValidIsvFee` in `types.ts`, called by both. `refs.ts` (`viva_<sessionId>`) imports nothing from the clients → client-safe. Stub session store is MODULE-LEVEL (another route/test's client sees earlier writes, like the real API); a `sessionId` containing `decline`/`abort` forces that outcome instead of the timed auto-approve; `stubState.reset()` in `beforeEach` or state bleeds across tests.
**Spec vs brief — the OpenAPI yaml won three times:** ISV endpoints live in `cloud.yaml`, not `isv.yaml`; abort is `DELETE /ecr/isv/v1/sessions/{id}` with a REQUIRED `cashRegisterId` query param (200/409 = re-fetch the session, 404 unknown, 403 real permission error); `searchDevices.merchantId` is required. `toCents()` routes through `round()` for consistency with `.claude/rules/payments.md`, not as a float fix — no double-rounding divergence could be reproduced, so don't document one.
**Prevention:** For any env-selected stub/real pair, put invariant validation in a third shared pure function both call. Re-derive request/response shapes from the downloaded spec, never from a track log's prose summary.

### 2026-08-30: Viva merchant connect (A2) — PartnerAccount.viva* + VivaTerminal, one VIVA_MODE for both clients
tags: entities=viva,partner-account,viva-terminal,connected-account,migration · files=packages/data/src/viva/accounts.ts,packages/data/src/viva/http-client.ts,packages/data/src/viva/index.ts,packages/data/prisma/schema.prisma · track=024
**Pattern:** Additive migration — 5 nullable `PartnerAccount.viva*` columns (snake_case `@map`, mirrors `mollie*`) + `VivaTerminal` (`terminalId @unique`; a physical terminal belongs to one site). `accounts.ts` generalises A1's token cache instead of duplicating it: `getAccessToken` takes a `scope` (default `ECR_SCOPE`), cache key `env:clientId:scope`; same host, different path prefix (`/isv/v1/*` vs `/ecr/isv/v1/*`). `getVivaAccountsClient()` shares `resolveMode()` with `getVivaClient()` so ONE `VIVA_MODE` switch can't leave one client stubbed and the other live.
**Spec vs brief (`isv.yaml`):** path is `/isv/v1/accounts[/{accountId}]`, not `/platforms/v1/accounts`; the create request accepts only `email`, `returnUrl`, `branding` — extra input fields (`legalName`, `taxNumber`, …) stay on the TS type but are dropped before the wire (test asserts they are `undefined` in the body); the retrieve response has a boolean `verified`, so `'rejected'` in `VivaAccountVerificationStatus` is webhook forward-compat — nothing in `accounts.ts` produces it.
**Prevention:** When a brief's TS interface has more fields than the API schema, keep them on the input type but add a test proving they never reach the wire.

### 2026-08-30: Viva collect rows (A3) — cardPresent condition, abandon can "stay processing", Viva branch inside getReservationPaymentStatus
tags: entities=reservation-state-machine,viva,collect,abandon,card-present · files=packages/data/src/reservation-machine.ts,packages/data/src/reservation-machine-apply.ts,packages/data/src/reservation-payment.ts,packages/data/src/viva-collect.integration.test.ts · track=024
**Pattern:** `'cardPresent'` in `CONDITIONS`, `'vivaSale'`/`'vivaAbort'` in `EFFECTS`; the `collect.start`/`collect.abandon` rows with `when: ['cardPresent']` sit ABOVE the QR/Mollie rows — `resolveTransition` takes the first full match, so row order alone routes the rail (track 018's edit-the-table doctrine). `computeConditions` derives `cardPresent` as a fact: `opts.collect.method === 'card'` on start, `isVivaPaymentRef(r.paymentRef)` on abandon.
**The one Mollie divergence:** Mollie's DELETE is synchronous so its abandon always resolves. Viva's abort works only before the card is read; after that (or when `cashRegisterId` can't be resolved — caller omitted it and the site has ≠ 1 `VivaTerminal`) `runCollectAbandonCard` POLLS `getSession` and has a THIRD outcome: "stays processing" (`paymentStatus: 'processing'`, no DB write) — reverting a possibly-authorised card would strand a charge the bank approved. The bug-revealing test gives the site a second `VivaTerminal` (defeats the single-terminal fallback) with an unresolved stub session and `abortPollMs: 0`.
**Reverify needed no changes:** `reverifyAndFinalizeReservation` dispatches on `getReservationPaymentStatus`'s normalized `succeeded`/`failed`, so the Viva branch there (approved→succeeded, declined/aborted→failed, pending/unknown→neither — a transient 404 must not revert a live tap) made abandon-after-approve finalize exactly like Mollie. Fee-guard test: seed a SITE-level `ServiceFee` (`percentage: 150`) so the real cascade produces a fee ≥ the sale and `assertValidIsvFee` throws — no guard mocking.
**Prevention:** A new provider needing the same abandon/reverify shape is a branch inside `getReservationPaymentStatus`, not a parallel copy of the generic caller. Never treat "unknown" provider state as failed.

## Analytics & fiscal reports

### 2026-07-10: getMonthlySourceSummary — rental cash-walk-in status shares RESERVATION_PAID_IN_CASH
tags: entities=analytics,rental-booking,status-constants · files=packages/data/src/analytics.ts,packages/data/src/reservation-status.ts
**Problem:** `RentalBooking.status` for cash walk-in rentals is the literal `'paid-in-cash'` — the same string as `RESERVATION_PAID_IN_CASH`; no `RENTAL_PAID_IN_CASH` constant exists. Online rentals use `RENTAL_COMPLETE` (`'complete'`).
**Solution:** Filter paid rentals with `status: { in: [RESERVATION_PAID_IN_CASH, RENTAL_COMPLETE] }`.
**Prevention:** Never invent a `RENTAL_PAID_IN_CASH` constant; check `reservation-status.ts` first.

### 2026-07-10: Order.paymentAmount — non-null only for post-payment status rows
tags: entities=order,analytics,fixtures · files=packages/data/src/analytics.ts,packages/data/src/test/fixtures.ts
**Observation:** `createTestOrder` defaults `paymentAmount: 30.0` regardless of status; production populates it on confirmation. Revenue queries filter by post-payment status and read `paymentAmount ?? 0` (not `totalPrice`), like the Reservation and RentalBooking takings pattern.
**Prevention:** Seed revenue assertions with explicit post-payment statuses; assert totals from `paymentAmount`.

### 2026-07-10: getMonthlyFiscalReport — site scoping for rental invoices via paymentRef-set join
tags: entities=invoice,fiscal-report,rental-booking,vat · files=packages/data/src/fiscal.ts
**Pattern:** `Invoice` has no `siteId`; reservation/order invoices scope via `reservation: { siteId }` / `order: { siteId }`, but rental invoices link only by `paymentRef`. Fetch the site's non-null `rentalBooking.paymentRef`s and add `paymentRef: { in: refs }` as a third OR clause (omitted when empty). `InvoiceLine.vatRate = null` buckets as rate 0 (PLATFORM reverse-charge lines). `refunds` is informational (from `refundedAt`/status, not credit notes) — same population as `getMonthlySourceSummary`.
**Prevention:** `fiscal.ts` needs only `RENTAL_REFUNDED`/`ORDER_REFUNDED`; importing more trips `no-unused-vars` at `--max-warnings 0`.

## Till & receipts

### 2026-07-23: closeEmployeeTill shared writer + today/carryOver window math
tags: entities=till,till-close,employee · files=packages/data/src/till.ts,packages/data/src/till.integration.test.ts · track=016
**Pattern:** `getOpenTill(siteId, employeeId, dayStart)` takes a caller-supplied venue-local `dayStart` (module stays tz-agnostic; callers use `siteDayBounds(buildSiteTimezone(site), now).start`). `today` = non-voided entries `settledAt > max(lastClose, dayStart)`; `carryOver` = `lastClose < settledAt <= dayStart`. The two windows partition `settledAt > lastClose`, so `today + carryOver` always equals the old since-last-close total (closed today ⇒ carryOver provably empty). `closeEmployeeTill` is the only `TillClose` writer; `closeAllOpenTills` loops it per non-zero employee — N closes for one source of truth instead of a `createMany` that duplicated the snapshot logic.
**Gotcha:** `getTillByEmployee`/`getEmployeeShiftItems` were spec'd unchanged, yet shared the `EmployeeTill` type — extending it would have forced bucket fields onto a civil-day report with no "day" notion. Split: `EmployeeTill`/`OpenTill` (bucketed) vs `EmployeeCashTotal` (plain `{employeeId,name,active,total,count}`).
**Prevention:** When a rework lists functions as "unchanged", check whether a shared TS type is used by both changed and unchanged functions before extending it — split types rather than leak fields.

## Integration test failures & fixes

### 2026-07-11: till integration test ESLint unused-var trap in destructuring + void binding
tags: entities=till,eslint,integration-test · files=packages/data/src/till.integration.test.ts
**Problem:** `npm run lint` at `--max-warnings 0` flags (1) destructuring `rentalItem` from `setup()` when the test never uses rentals; (2) binding `const zara = await mkEmp('Zara')` when the intent is only to create the roster row.
**Solution:** Destructure only what you use; call roster-only helpers without binding (`await mkEmp('Zara')`).
**Prevention:** Both patterns recur in every new test built on a shared `setup()` — check before lint.

### 2026-07-23: tsc --noEmit in packages/data — TS2209 is fixed; noUncheckedIndexedAccess conventions
tags: entities=typecheck,tsconfig,integration-test · files=packages/data/tsconfig.json,packages/data/src/till.integration.test.ts
**Problem:** Until `tsconfig.json` gained `rootDir: "."`, bare `npx tsc --noEmit` died on `TS2209: project root is ambiguous` before checking any file, so it silently type-checked nothing and pre-existing `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` violations accumulated.
**Solution:** `rootDir` is set and `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0 — it is a real gate now (no `typecheck` npm script; run it directly alongside `lint`). For array access in tests use `arr.find(...)!`, and for `fn.mock.calls[i][j]` add a small typed `call(fn, i)` helper that throws a clear message rather than sprinkling `!` (14 sites in one Viva test file paid for it).
**Prevention:** Run `npx tsc --noEmit` before claiming a packet typechecks; a `--rootDir .` workaround is no longer needed.

### 2026-08-30: Spying on the Viva stub singleton — vi.mock + vi.hoisted one memoized client
tags: entities=viva,vitest,stub-client,integration-test · files=packages/data/src/viva-collect.integration.test.ts,packages/data/src/viva/stub-client.ts · track=024
**Problem:** `getVivaClient()` returns a fresh object per call (the stub's store is module-level by design), so `vi.spyOn` on one instance cannot intercept the executor's own `getVivaClient()` calls.
**Solution:** `vi.mock('./viva', async (importOriginal) => { const client = actual.createStubVivaClient(); return { ...actual, getVivaClient: () => ({ ...client, createSale: (req) => { spy(req); return client.createSale(req) } }) } })` with `const { spy } = vi.hoisted(...)` — ONE memoized client shared by every call in the file; spread-copying is safe because the stub's methods don't close over `this`.
**Prevention:** Don't add a dynamic `await import('./viva')` after `vi.mock` to "guarantee" the mocked version — unnecessary (Vitest hoists `vi.mock` above every static import) and it breaks `tsc --noEmit` (`TS1309` top-level await) even though vitest runs it.
